title: The Per-Step Residue Law of the Non-Three-Square Density Error
description: Sequel to oq-03-oq-05-oq-01 (the density error E(N) = 6·excludedCount N − N is one-sided and Θ(log N)). The parent telescoped its recursion E(N) = E(⌈N/4⌉) + δ(N) inline; this entry isolates δ as a genuine function of N mod 8, proves the per-step law as a reusable lemma, the bounds −5 ≤ δ ≤ 0 with exact residue characterizations, and the key structural fact that the maximal cost δ = −5 (residue 7) cannot chain — because N ≡ 7 (mod 8) forces ⌈N/4⌉ even — while residue 6 (cost 4) does chain, explaining why the parent's all-(−4) family is the sustainable extremal one. Fully verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: delta: the per-step error contribution as an explicit function of the residue r = N mod 8, delta r = ⌊(r+3)/4⌋ − r, taking values 0,0,−1,−2,−3,−3,−4,−5 over r = 0..7. The parent's inline mod-8 increment, now a named function.

error_step: the PER-STEP LAW E(N) = E(⌈N/4⌉) + delta (N mod 8) for EVERY N, isolating the parent's inline telescoping of the oq-03-oq-05 recursion excludedCount N = N/8 + excludedCount ⌈N/4⌉ as a standalone, reusable lemma.

delta_nonpos / neg_five_le_delta: the per-step bounds −5 ≤ delta (N mod 8) ≤ 0; plus the residue dictionary delta_eq_zero_iff (r ∈ {0,1}), delta_eq_neg_four_iff (r = 6), delta_eq_neg_five_iff (r = 7).

quot_even_of_mod_seven: the SUSTAINABILITY OBSTRUCTION — when N ≡ 7 (mod 8) (the unique residue with maximal cost δ = −5), the next term ⌈N/4⌉ is even, hence not ≡ 7 (mod 8). So a −5 step is never immediately followed by another −5: the maximal single-step cost cannot sustain. Contrast mod6_chains: residue 6 (cost 4) chains to itself, the mechanism of the parent's extremal family. This explains why the sustainable extremal RATE is 4, not 5.

gap_step_le / gap_nonneg_and_step: the per-step descent inequality gap N ≤ gap ⌈N/4⌉ + 5 (with gap N = N − 6·excludedCount N ≥ 0 from the parent's six_excludedCount_le), the structural form behind the one-sided O(log N) bound.
prerequisites: excludedCount and excludedCount_rec (excludedCount N = N/8 + excludedCount ⌈N/4⌉) from the merged sibling oq-03-oq-05, imported and reused verbatim.
six_excludedCount_le (6·excludedCount N ≤ N for all N) from the direct parent oq-03-oq-05-oq-01, used for gap nonnegativity.
omega (Lean): discharges every residue-arithmetic, Nat-division, and ℤ-cast goal, including the mod-8 case analysis of delta and the quotient-parity facts.

overview.historicalContext: Legendre's three-square theorem excludes exactly the integers E = {4^a(8b+7)}. The sibling oq-03-oq-05 showed the density of E is 1/6 with a logarithmic error bound, and oq-03-oq-05-oq-01 settled the resulting dichotomy: the error E(N) = 6·excludedCount N − N is one-sided (E(N) ≤ 0 always) and genuinely unbounded, of order Θ(log N), realized by an explicit family a k with every descent step costing δ = −4. Both results hinge on telescoping the 4-descent recursion into E(N) = E(⌈N/4⌉) + δ(N) with δ a function of N mod 8 — but the parent performed this arithmetic inline. This entry extracts the per-step law as a reusable lemma and analyses the residue structure that governs the extremal rate, in particular why the maximal single-step cost (residue 7) cannot drive a faster family than residue 6.
overview.problemStatement: Isolate the per-step residue law E(N) = E(⌈N/4⌉) + δ(N mod 8) as a standalone lemma, establish the exact per-step bounds and residue characterizations of δ, and determine the structure of the extremal descent: given that a single step can cost 5 (residue 7), why is the sustainable extremal rate only 4 (residue 6)?
overview.text: A 154-line, fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file. It defines delta as a function of N mod 8, proves the per-step law error_step, the bounds and residue dictionary, the sustainability obstruction quot_even_of_mod_seven (with the companion mod6_chains), and the per-step descent inequality gap_step_le.
overview.proofStrategy: delta is defined directly as ⌊(r+3)/4⌋ − r. error_step rewrites excludedCount N via the imported excludedCount_rec, push_casts to ℤ, and closes the remaining division/remainder identity by omega (which natively understands N/8, ⌈N/4⌉ = (N+3)/4, and N mod 8). The bounds and residue characterizations are each one-line omega goals after unfolding delta, since omega case-splits on N mod 8 < 8. quot_even_of_mod_seven and mod6_chains are pure omega facts about how the residue and the quotient ⌈N/4⌉ interact (N = 8q+7 gives ⌈N/4⌉ = 2q+2, even). gap_step and gap_step_le are linarith consequences of error_step and the per-step bound; gap_nonneg_and_step adds the parent's six_excludedCount_le for nonnegativity.
keyInsights: The entire second-order behaviour of the three-square exceptional set reduces to a single mod-8 lookup function delta, whose eight values 0,0,−1,−2,−3,−3,−4,−5 simultaneously encode the sign (all ≤ 0 ⟹ one-sided) and the worst case.
The maximal step cost 5 occurs only at residue 7, and residue 7 forces an EVEN quotient ⌈N/4⌉, so it cannot be ≡ 7 again: a −5 step is structurally isolated and cannot sustain.

Residue 6 (cost 4) does chain to itself, so the sustainable extremal RATE is 4 — exactly the parent's family — even though larger single steps exist. This sharpens the intuition behind the Θ(log N) order.

Extracting the per-step law as a named lemma turns the parent's bespoke family computation into a general tool: any descent statement about the error now follows from error_step plus the residue dictionary.
prerequisites: The oq-03-oq-05 counting recursion for the excluded family E = {4^a(8b+7)}
Modular arithmetic mod 8 and integer division

conclusion.summary: The parent's one-sided Θ(log N) dichotomy for the non-three-square density error rests on a single residue law E(N) = E(⌈N/4⌉) + delta(N mod 8). This entry isolates that law as a reusable lemma, establishes the exact per-step bounds and residue dictionary, and shows the sustainable extremal rate is 4 (residue 6 chains) rather than 5 (residue 7 forces an even quotient and cannot chain).
conclusion.implications: Extracting the per-step law makes future descent arguments about the error mechanical, and the residue-7/residue-6 contrast clarifies the structure of the worst case — a prerequisite for any attempt at the exact Θ(log N) leading constant, which remains open precisely because the cost-5 steps, though isolated, still contribute O(1) bursts.
openQuestions: What is the exact leading constant of the Θ(log N) error? The cost-5 steps are isolated but each adds a bounded burst; pinning the constant requires counting how often residue 7 occurs along a descent.
Is there a descent with average cost strictly between 4 and 5 sustained over Θ(log N) steps, or is 4 the true asymptotic supremum rate?
Characterize exactly the set of N where the gap N − 6·excludedCount N attains its maximum at each scale [4^k, 4^{k+1}).
